right so the way I trade this, and I've been doing it for about two years now on the
micro nasdaq, MNQ, is I watch the opening range. so from 8:30 to 9:30 central time I
just let it build, I'm not touching anything, I'm literally just watching where the high
and the low of that first hour end up. that's my range.

then from 9:30 to 3:00 that's my window, that's when I'm actually looking for the trade.
what I want to see is price take out one side of that range, so it breaks the high or it
breaks the low, doesn't matter which, and then it comes back inside. that's the whole
thing. that's the setup. if it breaks the high and comes back in I'm short, if it breaks
the low and comes back in I'm long. the break can be just the wick, it doesn't have to
close outside, but the return back inside I want to see on a candle close. I wait for the
candle close on the 5 minute chart, I don't jump in early, I've lost too much money
jumping in early.

my stop is 25 points, that's just what it's always been. target is 50 points. one contract.
I do maximum 2 trades a day, if the first two don't work I'm done for the day, I walk away.
commission is 2 dollars a side and I usually get about 1 tick of slippage on these.

if I'm still in a trade at 3 I just flatten it, I'm out, I don't hold anything overnight
ever. and if a second signal fires while I'm already in something I just ignore it, I'm
only ever in one trade at a time. I don't scale in, I don't add, none of that.
